title: NarrationContext
description: The context assembler's output envelope: the ONLY state that may reach the narrator, alongside a ResolvedOutcome. LEAK AUDIT ANCHOR: true-sheet fields are structurally absent from this schema by design -- there is no place to put a real stat, difficulty, or hidden motive, and additionalProperties:false at every level means any attempt to smuggle one is a schema violation, not a style problem. CI leak audits validate every narrator payload against this file. Selection is deterministic (structured queries, never vector similarity); the assembler owns the token budget and the summarize-vs-quote policy. All declared fields are required; absence is expressed as null or [].

scene_manifest.description: The PERCEIVED scene -- the fog-of-warred subset of true scene state the player character can currently perceive. Same object the client tableau renders from: every entity here is guaranteed real and committed.

label_known.description: Location name as the player knows it; null if the place is unidentified.

known_sheet_slices.description: Chronicle-layer slices for entities relevant this turn: exact, immutable, authoritative facts of record (time, coin, inventory, wounds, named abilities, public guild rank, post-roll dice history). The narrator CANNOT contradict anything here. Never contains true-sheet values -- only facts already of record for the player.

salient_claims.description: Inquiry-layer claims selected deterministically (top-K by subject/location/recency). Fallible KNOWN: may be incomplete, outdated, or confidently wrong -- the narrator treats these as what the character believes, with provenance, never as world truth.

active_clocks.description: World clocks the player knows about that bear on this scene (timers, deadlines, pressure fronts). Only player-known clocks are ever assembled.

progress_text.description: Fictional progress stage ('cataloguing -> cross-referencing'), not digits.

canon_excerpts.description: Lore-bible / precedent-ledger material selected for this turn, each carrying the assembler's summarize-vs-quote decision.

source_ref.description: Stable reference into the lore bible or precedent ledger.

token_budget.description: The assembler-owned budget for the narrator call (~2-3k target per roadmap 4).

assembly.description: Assembler provenance (v1.1): version stamp, content hash, and the machine-readable trace of the LAST committed resolution -- always present so the narrator can never re-narrate the previous outcome (synthesis 2.4 section 7 / pitfall 4). Logged as an event by the caller.

content_hash.description: sha256 hex of the canonical envelope serialization (sorted keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii) computed with this field set to the empty string.

last_resolution.description: Trace of the previous committed resolution. Null ONLY at world start (no prior resolution exists); the section itself is never evicted.

resolution_trace.description: KNOWN-safe machine trace of one committed resolution: everything here is post-roll Chronicle data the player already saw. No true-sheet values can travel here.

action_summary.description: One-line factual summary of the resolved action (from the parsed approach, not prose).

dice_total.description: Post-roll total (rolls + modifiers); null when no roll occurred.

label_known.description: Name as the player knows it ('Warden Hessa') or a perceptual description ('a scarred guard') when unidentified.

category.description: Entity category (person, creature, item, feature) -- drives silhouettes and common-sense tier.

position.description: Tableau placement, normalized 0..1; null for ambient/off-tableau presences.

state_tags.description: Externally visible conditions only (wounded, asleep, armed). Never internal state.

claim.description: Full Inquiry claim with provenance (roadmap 3.3 claim schema). UI shows provenance, never confidence bars; confidence = evidence consistency, never truth-probability. Keep in lockstep with outcome.schema.json#/$defs/claim_write (duplicated deliberately, see README).

source.description: Named source ('Warden Hessa', 'the Ballad of Red Vermithrax').

observer.description: Who made the observation, when distinct from the source; null if unknown.

method.description: Acquisition method (witnessed, appraisal_ii, archive_research, rumor, inherited_journal, ...).

inheritance_status.description: original = first-hand this character; inherited = via journal/estate with qualifiers intact; inherited_incomplete = the note lost its qualifier (canonical wrong-intel mechanism).
